source.title: Loss Function Dynamics and Landscape for Deep Neural Networks Trained with Quadratic Loss
source.authors: M. Nakhodnov; M. Kodryan; E. Lobacheva; D. Vetrov

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests how learning rate, loss function, architecture, and L2 regularization relate to training dynamics and test error, using curvature and error metrics. It does not test the specific interventions or measurements named by the listed versions.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's own stated results about generalization and training conditions. Phase-diagram values visible only in figures are not reconstructed. Referenced studies and their results are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study reports learning-rate-dependent training phases and relationships between local curvature and test error. It does not measure any version's specified intervention or effect. In particular, its batch-gradient-norm curvature proxy is not V7's magnitude-aware weight-perturbation measure, and test error is not a direct measurement of the generalization gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors identify convergence, chaotic-equilibrium, and destabilized phases controlled by learning rate in scale-invariant networks, with related behavior in unconstrained VGG16BN. They conclude that the second-phase trajectory affects final generalization and that MSE requires longer training or greater model capacity for comparable convergence.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates loss-landscape phases and generalization in batch-normalized ConvNet and VGG16BN models; it does not reproduce the interventions or measurements in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate and its schedule change training phases and generalization; loss function affects convergence; L2 regularization changes VGG16BN stability, admissible learning-rate range, and reported generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Within the convergent first phase, increasing effective learning rate improves test performance and reduces local curvature; sufficiently high rates instead produce chance-level training performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate determines distinct training regimes in the tested scale-invariant ConvNet.

fits_no_version.finding: MSE runs on the full training set retain nonzero training error; on a 10% subset, test error is minimized at the highest learning rate in the first phase.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MSE convergence and generalization depend on learning rate and training-set size in this setup.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG16BN generalization is best near the highest first-phase learning rate; adding weight decay improves stability and reported test performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate and L2 regularization affect VGG16BN training stability and generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuning from the second phase at initial effective learning rate 0.001 yields better generalization than the best first-phase runs without a corresponding curvature improvement; Section 3.2 explicitly reports missing correlation between GM and test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local batch-gradient-norm curvature does not consistently track test performance across training histories.

record.problems: The main experiments use CIFAR10 without augmentation and a constrained scale-invariant ConvNet; VGG16BN results are reported in the appendix without dataset and loss specified in the text. Many plotted values are not stated numerically in the text. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying result rows identified. Figure-only values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects, small-data exceptions, excessive dropout, and joint dropout/weight-decay removal.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus generalization gaps, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites V7's original source as background, but its own curvature experiments do not test that version's specified measure. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not dispute the reported qualitative findings.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
A width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
A controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparison, including local-connectivity tests.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed or adapted training budgets.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons to norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: ConvNet
rows.size_stated: four convolutional layers; widths 32, 64, 128, 256; 10 output classes
rows.operation_detail: Varied effective learning rate during SGD training; no momentum or L2 regularization.
rows.measure: Test error/generalization as effective learning rate increases within the first phase
rows.value: Generalization grows monotonically with an increase in elr; best generalization is achieved in the widest optimum, assuming the network converges.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative result; exact test-error values are in figures and are not reconstructed.
rows.check: The qualitative learning-rate result is supported, but it measures no listed version. Optimum width here means landscape flatness, not network width in V2.

rows.subject: ConvNet
rows.size_stated: four convolutional layers; widths 32, 64, 128, 256; 10 output classes
rows.operation_detail: Varied effective learning rate into the third phase during SGD training.
rows.value: The train error becomes equivalent to random guess (90% in the case of 10 classes).
rows.note: This result concerns failure to converge in the high-learning-rate regime; the passage does not give a corresponding test-error value.
rows.check: The reported 90% training error concerns destabilization on natural labels, not fitting random labels or their held-out performance in V1.

rows.subject: ConvNet
rows.size_stated: four convolutional layers; widths 32, 64, 128, 256; 10 output classes
rows.operation_detail: Compared effective learning rates across the first phase of SGD training.
rows.value: None of the models converges to a zero error on the training set.
rows.note: Authors state MSE models converge more slowly than those trained with cross-entropy.
rows.check: The nonzero training-error result is supported for the tested MSE runs after 6000 iterations. It measures neither random-label memorization nor a network-width sweep.

rows.subject: ConvNet
rows.size_stated: four convolutional layers; widths 32, 64, 128, 256; 10 output classes
rows.operation_detail: Trained on a 10% subset of CIFAR10 with MSE loss.
rows.measure: Test error by effective learning rate
rows.value: The optimal effective learning rate in terms of test-set error corresponds to the highest learning rate in the first phase.
rows.note: The paper describes the relation qualitatively; exact test-error values are figure-only.
rows.check: The reported test-error optimum is supported, but learning-rate variation with MSE on a smaller dataset measures no listed version.

rows.subject: VGG16BN
rows.operation_detail: Varied learning rate without L2 regularization.
rows.value: Optimal generalization is achieved for the highest elr in the first phase, where curvature attains its minimum.
rows.note: In this section elr means the common learning rate; exact values are figure-only.
rows.check: The qualitative result is supported. Local curvature and test error do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap relationship.

rows.subject: VGG16BN
rows.operation_detail: Added L2 regularization with weight decay 10−4.
rows.value: The network becomes much more stable and the range of admissible elr expands; regularization has a positive effect on generalization, and the model converges to a wider optimum with better test quality Et.
rows.note: Qualitative comparison; exact test-quality values are figure-only.
rows.check: The reported stability and generalization improvement is supported. Adding L2 regularization alone tests neither V6's dropout comparisons nor V4's optimizer comparisons.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
